newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Safras sees Brazil soybean crop at 26.22 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Safras sees Brazil soybean crop at 26.22 mln tns.

text.p: Independent consultant Safras e Mercado said it was revising Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop down to 26.22 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 26.88 million tonnes.
The correction was mainly due to a sharp drop in the crop of key growing region Rio Grande do Sul following more than a month of drought in the region, said analyst Flavio Franca.
"It's a partial number because there were no rains last week, so it could be that the losses are bigger," Franca said.
Safras said it was revising its crop forecast for Rio Grande do Sul to 5.2 million tonnes from a previous 5.9 million tonnes.
It also saw a drop in productivity in Parana, the largest producing state, meaning the crop would come in at 6.7 million tonnes rather than previously forecast 6.79 million tonnes.
"Due to excessive rains in the region in January and February, productivity is slightly lower than last year," Franca said.
Safras expects to publish its next crop estimate in about 30 days' time, he added.
